subject: Cognitive Science
title: Communities of Practice
description: A quick win: understand Communities of Practice.

hook.text: New tailors start by ironing finished garments. Slowly they move to cutting, then sewing. Learning by belonging.

buildup.text: Lave and Wenger coined "communities of practice"—groups that learn through shared activity and identity.

discovery.text: Newcomers start at the periphery doing simple tasks and gradually move toward full participation.

twist.text: Knowledge lives in the community, not in textbooks. Lose the community and the knowledge fragments.

climax.text: Open-source software communities work this way: learn by contributing, grow by belonging.

punchline.text: You learn by joining, not just by studying.

quiz.question: What is legitimate peripheral participation?
options: Newcomers learn by doing simple tasks at the group's edge

details.summary: Lave and Wenger described learning as participation in communities of practice. Newcomers learn by legitimate peripheral participation, doing real tasks at the edges of a community, gradually moving toward fuller participation. Identity and belonging drive learning as much as content mastery.
details.whyItMatters: Communities of practice reframe learning as social identity change, not just information acquisition. You do not just learn what a programmer knows; you become a programmer.
takeaways: Learning happens through participation in communities
Newcomers start at the periphery and move inward
Identity transformation is a core part of learning

faq.question: What is legitimate peripheral participation?
faq.answer: Newcomers contribute to real work at the community's edges, doing simple but genuine tasks. A junior developer writes tests while seniors architect systems. Over time, participation deepens and responsibilities grow. The learning happens through doing real work, not through separate instruction.

faq.question: How do communities of practice form?
faq.answer: They emerge around shared domains of interest where members interact regularly and build communal resources. They can be intentionally cultivated by creating spaces for regular interaction, shared problem-solving, and knowledge exchange.
